captions.instagram:
How does a microphone work?

Your voice shoves a skin thinner than a hair, and a coil, a charged film or a chip of silicon turns that shiver into a few thousandths of a volt. Take a microphone apart in 3D, walk round it, and make it howl.

→ A stage microphone is a grille, a thin diaphragm, a copper coil and a magnet.
→ Sound is a wave of air pressure that pushes a thin diaphragm in and out.
→ In a dynamic microphone, a coil moving in a magnet’s gap generates the signal.
→ A condenser is a charged film a hair’s width from a metal plate: move the film and the voltage changes.
→ A MEMS microphone is the same idea etched in silicon, 3.5 mm long, and every phone has several.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/micclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does a microphone work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Your voice shoves a skin thinner than a hair, and a coil, a charged film or a chip of silicon turns that shiver into a few thousandths of a volt. Take a microphone apart in 3D, walk round it, and make it howl.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/micclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/micclear

In this video:
• A grille, a diaphragm, a coil and a magnet. A stage microphone is a tiny generator.
• Sound is pressure, and the diaphragm rides it. Sound is a wave of air pressure moving at 343 metres a second.
• Four ways to make a voltage. A dynamic moves a coil in a magnetic field.
• The shape of its hearing. Seal the back of a capsule and it hears all round.
• A whisper down a noisy cable. A microphone gives a few millivolts, so a preamp must boost it hundreds of times.
• Numbers, and the howl. A converter measures the signal 48,000 times a second and stores each measurement as a number.

Glassbox opens one box a day: an interactive model of how something works, plus the code behind it.
